evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v. Roterodamum: Roterodamum, Rotterdam
terms.comment: A town takes no preposition: Roterodāmum (to), Roterodāmī (in, at), Roterodāmō (from).

roterodamum.html: The long vowel puts the Latin stress where Dutch Rotterdam, stressed on its last syllable, has it, by the convention for modern names.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio, geographical section, with the authorities it cites (cited as M-O s.v.).

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus, edition of F. Benedict (1909), Latin–German, read in the digitization at columbia.edu (cited as Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v.); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
